exams.quote: shall be able to pass the standard examination prescribed by the State Board of Podiatry. The standard examination shall consist of tests in practical, theoretical, and physiological podiatry, in the anatomy and physiology of the human foot, and in pathology as applied to podiatry

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of any offense involving moral turpitude
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of any offense involving moral turpitude, in which case the record of conviction or a certified copy thereof certified by the clerk of the court or by the judge in which court the conviction is had shall be conclusive evidence of such conviction

disciplinary_grounds.description: Unprofessional conduct including fraud, fee-splitting, misleading advertising, or employment of unlicensed practitioners
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Unprofessional conduct including any conduct of a character likely to deceive or defraud the public, lending his or her license to any person, the employment of 'cappers,' or 'steerers' to obtain business, 'splitting' or dividing a fee with any person or persons, the obtaining of any fee or compensation by fraud or misrepresentation, employing directly or indirectly any suspended or unlicensed podiatrist to do any professional work, fraudulent or misleading advertising

disciplinary_grounds.description: Obtaining a license or certificate by fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Obtaining a license or certificate by fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation, whether knowingly or unknowingly practiced on the board

disciplinary_grounds.description: Suffering from a contagious or infectious disease
disciplinary_grounds.quote: When the holder of a license or certificate is suffering from a contagious or infectious disease

disciplinary_grounds.description: Gross incompetency, willful or wanton negligence, or repeated negligence in practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Gross incompetency, wilful or wanton negligence, or repeated negligence in the practice of podiatry

disciplinary_grounds.description: Intemperance in use of intoxicating liquors or narcotics to extent unfitting for practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Intemperance in the use of intoxicating liquors or narcotics to such an extent as to unfit the holder of the license for the proper practice of podiatry

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to renew license and pay any penalty prescribed
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to renew his or her license and pay any penalty prescribed in this article

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to comply with continuing education requirements
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to comply with continuing education requirements prescribed in this article

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating any rule or regulation promulgated by the board
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating any rule or regulation promulgated by the board

disciplinary_grounds.description: Disciplinary action taken by another state based on similar acts
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Disciplinary action taken by another state based upon acts by a licensee similar to acts described in this section which results in suspension or revocation of a license or certificate to practice podiatry in another state

disciplinary_grounds.description: Sexual misconduct including sexual relationships, advances, or inappropriate viewing
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Sexual misconduct including, but not limited to, any or all of the following: Engaging in or soliciting a consensual or nonconsensual sexual relationship when a podiatrist-patient relationship exists. Making sexual advances, requesting sexual favors, and engaging in other verbal conduct or physical contact of a sexual nature with a patient. Intentionally viewing a completely or partially disrobed patient in the course of treatment if the viewing is not related to patient diagnosis or treatment according to current practice standards

disciplinary_grounds.description: Any other misconduct defined by the board
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any other misconduct defined by the board

definition_quote.value: The diagnosis and medical or surgical or mechanical or manipulative or electrical treatment of any ailment of the human foot or ankle and the surgical treatment of ailments of the human foot or ankle limited anatomically to the foot or ankle. The practice of podiatry shall include the amputation of the toes and other parts of the foot and ankle, but shall not include any amputation above the Chopart joint, total ankle arthroplasty, or the administration of any anesthetic other than local. A podiatrist may prescribe drugs that relate specifically to the scope of practice authorized herein.
